title: Basic Calculator II
statement:
Given a string `s` which represents an expression, evaluate this expression and return its value. 

The integer division should truncate toward zero.

You may assume that the given expression is always valid. All intermediate results will be in the range of `[-2^31, 2^31 - 1]`.

The expression contains only non-negative integers, '+', '-', '*', '/' operators and empty spaces ' '. There are no parentheses.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string `s`.
outputFormat: A single integer: the evaluated value.

starterCode.python:
s = input().strip()
# Write your solution here
# Use a stack to keep track of numbers to be summed
